entries.reason: The port declares no such owner, so nothing can be reached through it. Measured in this tree: grep for '^@protocol NSTextContentManagerDelegate' and '^@interface NSTextContentManagerDelegate' over every .h and .m under packages/a/apple-backports returns nothing - not a protocol declaration and not a class - so a caller holding an id<NSTextContentManagerDelegate> has no protocol to conform to or cast to. This row said `implemented` while its siblings in the same file and the protocol row itself said `absent`, and the measured state does not support `implemented`. The SELECTORS are not missing from the tree - they are the port's own, on NSTextContentStorage15.m - but that is a different API: these are the methods a caller-supplied delegate implements, and a port class that happens to answer them is not the protocol being carried. The measured behaviour stays in facts/UIKit/NSTextContent15.md; what is absent is the owner, and this row now says so. Found by v-swift2's registry-vs-built measurement and settled here; the disagreement was inside one package and, for five of the seven, inside one file.

A caller that wants markers in the text this port produces has none to get: -enumerateTextElementsFromLocation:options:usingBlock: and -textElementsForRange: return the NSTextParagraphs the document is cut into, and no NSTextListMarker is among them
entries.source: the property is declared on NSTextContentStorage in the 26.2 UIKit surface, which coordination/corpus/sdk-26.2-surface.tsv records at line 142425 as NSTextContentStorage.includesTextListMarkers, kind property, introduced 26.0, via own, and at :142427 and :142536 the same property on NSTextList and UIWritingToolsCoordinator; it is absent from the iPhoneOS16.4 SDK the build compiles against, which is why the port answers it as a written accessor rather than as a synthesised property. What this class carries is measured on the armv7-apple-ios6.1.3 objects built from packages/a/apple-backports/UIKit/NSTextContentStorage15.m and UIKit26_0.m and read with otool -ov from __objc_classlist and __charon_catlist
entries.reason: not carried on this class, and the row was naming the wrong one: the 26.2 UIKit surface has includesTextListMarkers on three classes - NSTextContentStorage, NSTextList and UIWritingToolsCoordinator - and the port answers the NSTextList one only, in @implementation NSTextList (CharonUIKit26) at UIKit26_0.m:378, which ios26.json carries as its own row NSTextList.includesTextListMarkers. What is missing here is not the spelling but the behaviour, and it is a text-production rule the storage does not have: the port's storage is the document over an NSTextStorage and its elements are NSTextParagraphs (NSTextContentStorage15.m:1-9 and :34-40), so it never produces a text list marker at all - NSTextListMarker is not a class the port carries, only its seventeen enumerated constants are (registry/UIKit/measured-constants.json), and UIWritingToolsCoordinator, the third class the SDK puts the property on, is a class the port does not implement. A stored flag would answer YES to a question about text this storage generates, which is the fiction, so the flag is not written. That is the difference from the NSTextList row beside it: a list is nothing but its markers, so there the getter returning what the setter stored is the whole of the property
